2.text: make an assault while they are there. Then there is a small old woman,

3.text: quite blind, and armed with an iron whip. She swings her whip all night

4.text: long, here and there before my entrance. It frightens away the keˊlet, and
4.as_typed: long, here and there before my entrance. It frightens away the {ke'let}, and

5.text: prevents them from making an attack. After that, two big polar owls are

6.text: put on the watch around this house. They have iron beaks and iron wings.

7.text: Their beaks are very sharp. When the keˊlᴇ, the murderer, who is wont
7.as_typed: Their beaks are very sharp. When the {ke'le_}, the murderer, who is wont

8.text: to make assaults, comes to the house and wants to enter it, they strike at

9.text: him with their beaks, wound him severely, and peck out his eyes. His blood

10.text: flows away far into the wilderness. Then he feels afraid, and leaves off.

12.text: (b) I make the house of human people into a closed iron ball. It has

13.text: no entrance and no windows, and there is only a small vent-hole on top.

14.text: I put around this hole a sharp knife-blade. No keˊlᴇ can enter through it;
14.as_typed: I put around this hole a sharp knife-blade. No {ke'le_} can enter through it;

15.text: no source of death knows anything about it. In the evening, in the time

16.text: for sleep, something bad will try to attack the house. One will say, “Let

17.text: us enter this house!” — “Yes, let us do it!” They go around the house,

18.text: looking for the entrance. There is no entrance, and they cannot find it.

19.text: “Oh! what side shall we try? It is wonderful. We cannot find the entrance.

20.text: Let us do it from below. We will enter it through the ground of the outer

21.text: tent!” They dive into the ground, but have to re-appear on the other side.

22.text: It is impossible to enter, because the house is all iron. They come again

23.text: to the front. “Where shall we try it, oh! I hear the people’s voices inside.

24.text: There now! Let me try and climb to the roof.” One of them climbs to

25.text: the roof and sees the vent-hole. “Oh! I have found it! Here is a place to

26.text: make an attempt. Come, now! lower me down this hole, upon a rope.”

27.text: They lower him down; but the hole is narrow, and armed with a sharp blade.

28.text: It cuts him all over. The blood spurts out, even the intestines come out,

29.text: and he cannot endure the pain. “Oh! oh! Haul me up! I shall die! I

30.text: have bruised and lacerated my whole body.” They haul in the rope. His

31.text: bowels and intestines are all out, and he is covered with blood. “Oh! let us

32.text: go away! It is too bad. My body is all cut to pieces. I have nearly met

33.text: my death here. We do not want it.” They leave the game and go away.

35.text: (c) If I am afraid to sleep alone, I say that I have cut off the left half

36.text: of a female dog’s body, and I gather the dog’s blood in the hollow of my

37.text: hand. In this blood I go to sleep. Who can see where I am? That’s all.

38.text: Told by Scratching-Woman (man) at Mariinsky Post, 1900.
